title: Export a video for YouTube
summary: Use the YouTube preset on the Deliver page to render your timeline to a file.

steps.say: Click Deliver on the bottom bar of the window to open the Deliver page.

checks.prompt: Is the Deliver page active, with the Deliver icon highlighted on the bottom bar and Render Settings on the left?

hints: The page buttons are icons with labels in a row along the very bottom edge. Deliver is one of them.
You can also press Shift 8 to jump straight to the Deliver page.
steps.why: Every task in Resolve belongs to a page, and the Deliver page has the tools for this lesson.

steps.say: In Render Settings at the top left, click the YouTube preset.

check.prompt: Is the YouTube preset highlighted at the top of Render Settings?

hints: The presets are a row of tiles across the top of Render Settings. Scroll the row sideways if needed.
If you cannot find it, choose H.264 or the Custom Export preset with MP4 format instead.
steps.why: The preset fills in format and codec settings that YouTube handles well.

steps.say: Check that the resolution matches your timeline, for example 1080p.
hints: The YouTube preset has a resolution menu next to it. Pick 1080p for most videos.
Pick 2160p only if your footage and timeline are 4K.
steps.why: Exporting at the timeline resolution keeps the picture sharp without wasting space.

steps.say: Type a file name, then click Browse to choose where to save it.

check.prompt: Is a file name filled in and a save folder shown in Render Settings?

hints: The Filename and Location fields are near the top of Render Settings.
Pick a folder you can find later, such as Videos or Desktop.
steps.why: Choosing the folder now saves searching for the finished file later.

steps.say: Click Add to Render Queue at the bottom of Render Settings.

checks.prompt: Is there a new job listed in the Render Queue on the right?

hints: Scroll Render Settings down if the button is hidden below the settings.
This only creates a job. Nothing is exported until the next step.
steps.why: The queue lets you line up several exports and run them together.

steps.say: Click Render All in the Render Queue on the right.

check.prompt: Is a render progress bar or percentage showing in the Render Queue or under the viewer?

hints: Render All is the button at the bottom of the Render Queue panel.
If the Render Queue is hidden, click Render Queue at the top right of the window.
steps.why: Render All starts writing the video file.

steps.say: Wait until the job says it is complete, then open the folder to find your video.

checks.prompt: Does the render job show as completed, with no progress bar running?

hints: Rendering time depends on the length of the video and your computer.
Open File Explorer and go to the folder you chose under Location.
steps.why: Checking the finished file confirms the export worked before you upload it.
